narrative:
The 2026 Minnesota Twins opened the season with cautious optimism, but April proved to be a grind from the start. A 1-3 March gave way to a 13-15 April that featured some of the season's most dramatic individual moments — both uplifting and deflating. Ryan Jeffers provided a grand slam to remember on April 23rd, but the bullpen was already showing cracks, and the offense's inconsistency kept Minnesota treading water through the early weeks.

May and June brought more of the same mixed signals. The Twins went a combined 27-28 over those two months, with Austin Martin emerging as a bright spot and Kody Clemens flashing genuine power. But the pitching staff was a persistent source of heartbreak — Taylor Rogers surrendering a go-ahead homer in late May, Joe Ryan getting ambushed by Yordan Alvarez's grand slam in June, and reliever Eric Orze making cameos in several of the season's most painful moments. Anthony Banda's struggles in late June epitomized a roster that could never quite string together enough consistency to build a meaningful cushion.

July provided the season's brightest chapter. Minnesota went 15-9, its best month by a wide margin, powered by a rejuvenated Royce Lewis and a remarkable Kody Clemens grand slam on July 30th that stands as the single most impactful positive play of the season. That late-July surge rekindled hope, but August brought a sobering 10-17 collapse that effectively buried the Twins' postseason aspirations. The momentum evaporated as the lineup went cold and the pitching staff wore down.

September has been a study in pride-preserving baseball. At 11-13 through mid-September, the Twins are playing out the string but not without fight — Walker Jenkins has provided a glimpse of future upside with a home run, and Royce Lewis continues to flash his talent. At 77-85, Minnesota's season will not end with a playoff appearance, but the July surge and the individual performances of Clemens, Lewis, and Martin give the organization genuine building blocks to evaluate as the final games approach.

chapters.title: Rocky Beginnings
chapters.description: Minnesota stumbles through April, mixing individual heroics like Jeffers' grand slam with costly pitching meltdowns that leave the team hovering near .500.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: May brings flashes of offense from Austin Martin and Brooks Lee, but late-game bullpen failures — including Taylor Rogers' crushing blown save — keep the Twins from gaining ground.

chapters.title: June Turbulence
chapters.description: A .500 June features Kody Clemens' emerging power and clutch contributions, but Joe Ryan and Anthony Banda surrender critical homers that prevent Minnesota from breaking through.

chapters.title: The July Surge
chapters.description: The Twins' best month arrives on the strength of Royce Lewis' return and Kody Clemens' walk-off grand slam, their most impactful play of the entire season.

chapters.title: Fading Down the Stretch
chapters.description: August's 10-17 collapse extinguishes playoff hopes, and September becomes a showcase for young talent like Walker Jenkins as the Twins play out a disappointing 77-85 campaign.
